title: Osero's execution capacity is split between a Prime Foundation and a contracted development company
content:
Two adjacent parameters in the Agent Creation Instance Configuration define Osero's off-chain structure. A.6.1.1.7.2.1.1.3.1.1.5 names the Osero Foundation as "the Prime Foundation associated with Osero," whose "mandate is to support the development, growth, and adoption of Osero." A.6.1.1.7.2.1.1.3.1.1.6 adds that "Stablewatch is a development company that provides services to the Osero Foundation."

The chain has three links, not two: the Agent (an Atlas construct with onchain accounts), the Foundation (a legal entity holding a mandate), and the development company (a vendor engaged by the Foundation). Each boundary is a substitution point — the development company can be replaced without touching the Foundation, and the Foundation's mandate is defined in the Artifact rather than in a private contract.

The direction of the service relationship matters. Stablewatch contracts with the Foundation, not with Osero the Agent, so the Artifact does not need to describe or approve the engineering arrangement. What the Artifact fixes is only the mandate; how it is discharged is delegated.

The trade-off is transparency. Because the vendor relationship sits one level below what the Artifact specifies, the actual builders of Osero are named but their terms of engagement are outside the governed text.
description: Osero Foundation holds the Atlas mandate to support development, growth and adoption; Stablewatch supplies services to the Foundation rather than to the Agent directly.
